messages:
Marta: Quick sync — Acme Financial POC kickoff. They want a multi-language example (Java + .NET + Rust) for streaming inference that demonstrates function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs. Do we have a runnable sample we can hand them this week?

Ryan: @marta we have node/python streaming end-to-end samples, but not a polished java/.net/rust repo. I can assemble snippets. Timeline? :calendar:

Samir: Heads-up — procurement flagged two enterprise blockers: 1) they require an SSO + KMS flow in the POC; 2) they need a pricing estimate for a 2-week trial at ~200 qps steady, peaks to 500 qps. Also security questionnaire coming.

Dev-bot: issue created RW-4623 presales/multi-sdk-streaming-samples (assignee: ryan).

Marta: OK on blockers. For the sample we should show: websocket handshake, backpressure handling, function-call events (tool invocation), and an example of prefix/kv caching to reduce tokens. If we can include a short canary fallback (hosted -> lightweight quantized variant) that'd be 👍.

Ryan: Copy. For Java/.NET, websocket + async callback is the recommended path — SSE is 1-way and doesn’t handle tool callbacks well. Example event payload we plan to surface:

```json
{
  "event": "tool_call",
  "tool": "lookup_customer",
  "args": {"customer_id": "12345"},
  "request_id": "req_abc123"
}
```

Ryan: The client will receive that, call their adapter, then post a tool_result event back to the runtime. We'll include sample code for sending/receiving these events.

Samir: For pricing: we should propose two options in a one-pager — Hosted POC estimate (usage + burst buffer) and Dedicated short-term trial (reserved for duration). I can draft numbers if you give the qps→tokens assumptions.

Marta: We'll assume average 32 tokens/response, 8 tokens/request, so ~40 tokens per round. At 200 qps continuous for 14 days that's ~200 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 14 * 40 tokens — but for the one-pager a high-level cost band is fine. Ryan, can you confirm batching/caching assumptions?

Ryan: Yes — with KV caching on prefixes we can cut token usage by ~30% on repetitive prompts. Also recommend batching when latency target allows. I'll add a small table in the runbook with cost delta examples (no hard invoice).

Dev-bot: uploaded sample checklist -> https://git.redwood/samples/multi-sdk-stream/checklist.md

Marta: Security Q: Acme asked about ephemeral creds for the SDKs and audit logs for tool activity. We should provide a minimal architecture diagram and a snippet showing how to rotate short-lived creds in Java.

Ryan: I'll add a Java snippet for STS-based short-lived token exchange and a .NET equivalent. Also include guidance for encrypting tool args at rest (KMS).

Samir: Suggest we propose a 30–45 minute live technical walkthrough with their eng lead and security on Tuesday. We'll demo the sample and answer the questionnaire live. I can own scheduling.

Marta: Great. Action items: (1) Ryan — create multi-lang repo with websocket handshake + tool_call flow + structured JSON examples + README (ETA: Tue EOD). (2) Samir — draft pricing one-pager + coordinate Q/A (ETA: Mon noon). (3) Marta — prep security diagram and questionnaire answers (ETA: Mon EOD).

Ryan: Acknowledged, starting branch presales/multi-sdk. Will ping when initial samples pushed.

Samir: I'll book the walkthrough slot after Ryan confirms sample availability.

Marta: Thanks team. If anyone runs into infra rate-limit questions ping eng-runtime. :rocket:

Ryan: one quick note — for Rust we can point to the low-level websocket client + small adapter snippet rather than a full maintained SDK; faster to deliver.

Marta: Fine — pragmatic is better for POC.

Dev-bot: reminder: RW-4623 due in 5 business days.

Samir: Perfect, I'll update the CRM with the POC plan and attach checklist link.

Marta: Closing thread for now, will reopen if scheduling changes. Thanks all.
